title.suggested: Tom Allen and Joe Goss in Training for September Fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported on Tom Allen and Joe Goss in training for their September 7 championship fight. Interviewed in St. Louis, Allen swore the match was on the level and predicted Goss would break down.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, July 16, 1876', page 4.

facts.fact: About ten days before July 16, 1876, at the close of their engagement at the Comique, Allen and his trainer Jack Madden left St. Louis for Cincinnati to train for the Goss fight
Allen and Joe Goss signed articles at Cincinnati for a fight for the championship of America, set for September 7, 1876
While in St. Louis, Allen told a Globe-Democrat reporter at the Olive Street Hotel that the Goss match was on the 'dead level' and that the fighting ground, a farm, had already been selected
Allen predicted how the fight with Goss would go
facts.quote: It will be the liveliest scrap you ever saw for the first twenty minutes. He's a game 'un, and clever, but a little slow. He'll stand punishment like a bull-dog, and the only way you can lick him is to blind him.

notes: The article says Allen and Goss had earlier 'fought a draw in three rings'.
